title: Month-over-month change

WITH m AS (
    SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(ShipDate), MONTH(ShipDate), 1) AS MonthStart,
           SUM(FreightCharge) AS Total
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    GROUP BY DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(ShipDate), MONTH(ShipDate), 1)
)
SELECT MonthStart, Total,
       LAG(Total) OVER (ORDER BY MonthStart)         AS PrevMonth,
       Total - LAG(Total) OVER (ORDER BY MonthStart) AS Change
FROM m
ORDER BY MonthStart;

title: Top 3 customers per region by freight charge

sql:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT p.Region, p.CustomerName, SUM(e.FreightCharge) AS TotalFreightCharge,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.Region ORDER BY SUM(e.FreightCharge) DESC) AS rn
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
    JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS p ON p.CustomerID = e.CustomerID
    GROUP BY p.Region, p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName
)
SELECT Region, CustomerName, TotalFreightCharge
FROM t
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY Region, rn;

title: Monthly rank of carriers
q: For each month, rank carriers by their total freight charge that month and show only the top carrier (ties included).
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT MONTH(e.ShipDate) AS MonthNo, d.CarrierName, SUM(e.FreightCharge) AS Total,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY MONTH(e.ShipDate) ORDER BY SUM(e.FreightCharge) DESC) AS rnk
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
    JOIN retail_logistics.Carriers AS d ON d.CarrierID = e.CarrierID
    GROUP BY MONTH(e.ShipDate), d.CarrierID, d.CarrierName
)
SELECT MonthNo, CarrierName, Total
FROM m
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY MonthNo;

title: Repeat shipments within N days
q: Find shipments that happened within @Days days of the same customer's previous shipment. Use @Days = 145. Show customer, previous date, current date and gap.
sql:
DECLARE @Days int = 145;

WITH v AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, ShipmentID, ShipDate,
           LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID) AS PrevDate
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
)
SELECT CustomerID, PrevDate, ShipDate,
       DATEDIFF(day, PrevDate, ShipDate) AS GapDays
FROM v
WHERE PrevDate IS NOT NULL
  AND DATEDIFF(day, PrevDate, ShipDate) <= @Days
ORDER BY CustomerID, ShipDate;
how: LAG finds the previous shipment and DATEDIFF measures the gap. A variable makes the window easy to change. Repeat-activity checks like this are a common interview question.

title: Constraint vs trigger vs app
q: Write a query that shows, for each table, how many PK, FK, UNIQUE, CHECK and DEFAULT constraints it has.
sql:
SELECT OBJECT_NAME(parent_object_id) AS TableName,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'PK' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS PK,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'F'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FK,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'UQ' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS UQ,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'C'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS CK,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'D'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DF
FROM sys.objects
WHERE type IN ('PK', 'F', 'UQ', 'C', 'D')
  AND SCHEMA_NAME(schema_id) = 'retail_logistics'
GROUP BY parent_object_id
ORDER BY TableName;
how: Prefer declarative constraints: they are faster, always applied, and help the optimizer. Use triggers only for cross-table rules, and application checks for friendly messages.

title: Shipment chain for one customer
q: Starting from customer 1's first shipment, use a recursive CTE to walk forward through that customer's shipments in date order, with a step number.
sql:
WITH Ordered AS (
    SELECT ShipmentID, ShipDate,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID) AS rn
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    WHERE CustomerID = 1
), Chain AS (
    SELECT ShipmentID, ShipDate, rn, 0 AS Step
    FROM Ordered
    WHERE rn = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT o.ShipmentID, o.ShipDate, o.rn, c.Step + 1
    FROM Ordered AS o
    JOIN Chain AS c ON o.rn = c.rn + 1
)
SELECT ShipmentID, ShipDate, Step
FROM Chain
ORDER BY Step;

title: MAXRECURSION
q: Generate numbers 1 to 200 with a recursive CTE. (The default limit is 100 levels.)
sql:
WITH N AS (
    SELECT 1 AS n
    UNION ALL
    SELECT n + 1 FROM N WHERE n < 200
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS HowMany, MAX(n) AS LastNumber
FROM N
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 200);

title: Month-over-month with a calendar
q: For all 12 months of 2024 (even empty ones), show total freight charge, previous month's total and growth %.
sql:
WITH Months AS (
    SELECT CAST('2024-01-01' AS date) AS m
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD(month, 1, m) FROM Months WHERE m < '2024-12-01'
), Totals AS (
    SELECT mo.m, ISNULL(SUM(e.FreightCharge), 0) AS Total
    FROM Months AS mo
    LEFT JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
           ON e.ShipDate >= mo.m AND e.ShipDate < DATEADD(month, 1, mo.m)
    GROUP BY mo.m
)
SELECT m AS MonthStart, Total,
       LAG(Total) OVER (ORDER BY m) AS PrevTotal,
       CAST(100.0 * (Total - LAG(Total) OVER (ORDER BY m))
            / NULLIF(LAG(Total) OVER (ORDER BY m), 0) AS decimal(6,1)) AS GrowthPct
FROM Totals
ORDER BY m;

title: Org-chart style hierarchy with path
q: Build a small hierarchy in a table variable (region head > team > customer) and list it with a recursive CTE, showing each level and a path like Head > North > Olivia.
sql:
DECLARE @Org TABLE (NodeID int, ParentID int NULL, NodeName nvarchar(100));
INSERT INTO @Org VALUES (0, NULL, N'Head');
INSERT INTO @Org
SELECT DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Region), 0, Region
FROM retail_logistics.Customers
GROUP BY Region;
INSERT INTO @Org
SELECT 100 + p.CustomerID, r.NodeID, p.CustomerName
FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p
JOIN @Org AS r ON r.NodeName = p.Region
WHERE p.CustomerID <= 6;

WITH Tree AS (
    SELECT NodeID, NodeName, 0 AS Lvl, CAST(NodeName AS nvarchar(400)) AS PathText
    FROM @Org
    WHERE ParentID IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT o.NodeID, o.NodeName, t.Lvl + 1,
           CAST(t.PathText + N' > ' + o.NodeName AS nvarchar(400))
    FROM @Org AS o
    JOIN Tree AS t ON o.ParentID = t.NodeID
)
SELECT NodeID, Lvl, PathText
FROM Tree
ORDER BY PathText;

title: MERGE: sync a staging table
q: Sync customer regions from a staging list: update regions that changed, insert new customers, and report each action.
sql:
DECLARE @Stage TABLE (CustomerID int, CustomerName nvarchar(80), CustomerCode varchar(20), Region varchar(10));
INSERT INTO @Stage
SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerCode, CASE WHEN Region = 'East' THEN 'West' ELSE 'East' END
FROM retail_logistics.Customers WHERE CustomerID = 1          -- region change
UNION ALL
SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerCode, Region
FROM retail_logistics.Customers WHERE CustomerID = 2          -- no change
UNION ALL
SELECT 301, N'New Customer', 'LC-000301', 'North';     -- new

MERGE retail_logistics.Customers AS t
USING @Stage AS s
   ON t.CustomerID = s.CustomerID
WHEN MATCHED AND t.Region <> s.Region THEN
    UPDATE SET t.Region = s.Region
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN
    INSERT (CustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerCode, Region)
    VALUES (s.CustomerID, s.CustomerName, s.CustomerCode, s.Region)
OUTPUT $action AS ActionTaken, inserted.CustomerID, deleted.Region AS OldRegion, inserted.Region AS NewRegion;

title: Generate test rows with a set
q: Insert 20 test shipments for customer 1 in one statement, one per day starting 2025-01-01, with IDs 1001-1020.

WITH N AS (
    SELECT TOP (20) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n
    FROM sys.all_objects
)
INSERT INTO retail_logistics.Shipments
    (ShipmentID, CustomerID, ShipmentReference, ShipmentCategory, Status, FreightCharge,
     DeclaredPackages, ShipDate, DispatchedAt, RecordedAt, CarrierID)
SELECT 1000 + n, 1, CONCAT(N'RET-TEST-', n), 'A', 'Open', 100, 1,
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01' AS date)),
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01 09:00' AS datetime2(3))),
       DATEADD(day, n - 1, CAST('2025-01-01 09:01 +00:00' AS datetimeoffset(3))), 1
FROM N;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS TestRows, MIN(ShipDate) AS FirstDate, MAX(ShipDate) AS LastDate
FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
WHERE ShipmentID BETWEEN 1001 AND 1020;

title: Isolation levels
q: Name SQL Server's transaction isolation levels and the problem each one prevents. Show the current level.
sql:
SELECT CASE transaction_isolation_level
         WHEN 1 THEN 'READ UNCOMMITTED' WHEN 2 THEN 'READ COMMITTED'
         WHEN 3 THEN 'REPEATABLE READ'  WHEN 4 THEN 'SERIALIZABLE'
         WHEN 5 THEN 'SNAPSHOT' END AS IsolationLevel
FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions
WHERE session_id = @@SPID;
how: READ UNCOMMITTED allows dirty reads. READ COMMITTED (the default) prevents dirty reads. REPEATABLE READ also prevents non-repeatable reads. SERIALIZABLE also prevents phantom rows. SNAPSHOT reads a consistent version without blocking writers. Higher isolation means fewer anomalies but more blocking.

q: What are statistics, and why do they matter? Show the statistics objects on Shipments.
sql:
SELECT s.name AS StatName, s.auto_created, sp.rows, sp.last_updated
FROM sys.stats AS s
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_db_stats_properties(s.object_id, s.stats_id) AS sp
WHERE s.object_id = OBJECT_ID('retail_logistics.Shipments');
how: Statistics describe how values are spread in a column (a histogram). The optimizer uses them to estimate row counts (cardinality) and choose plans. Out-of-date statistics cause bad estimates and slow queries; UPDATE STATISTICS refreshes them.

title: Transaction log and recovery models

title: Self join: next shipment
q: Pair each shipment with the same customer's next shipment. Show both IDs and dates.
sql:
WITH n AS (
    SELECT ShipmentID, CustomerID, ShipDate,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID) AS rn
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
)
SELECT a.CustomerID, a.ShipmentID, a.ShipDate,
       b.ShipmentID AS NextID, b.ShipDate AS NextDate
FROM n AS a
JOIN n AS b ON b.CustomerID = a.CustomerID AND b.rn = a.rn + 1
ORDER BY a.CustomerID, a.ShipDate;

title: Joins that multiply rows
q: Show each customer's total shipment freight charge and total number of packages. Make sure the freight charge is not double counted.
sql:
SELECT p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName,
       ISNULL(ch.TotalFreightCharge, 0) AS TotalFreightCharge,
       ISNULL(li.ShipmentPackages, 0) AS ShipmentPackages
FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p
LEFT JOIN (SELECT CustomerID, SUM(FreightCharge) AS TotalFreightCharge
           FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
           GROUP BY CustomerID) AS ch ON ch.CustomerID = p.CustomerID
LEFT JOIN (SELECT e.CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS ShipmentPackages
           FROM retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS r
           JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e ON e.ShipmentID = r.ShipmentID
           GROUP BY e.CustomerID) AS li ON li.CustomerID = p.CustomerID
ORDER BY TotalFreightCharge DESC;
how: If you join Shipments and ShipmentPackages first and then SUM(FreightCharge), a shipment with 2 packages has its freight charge counted twice (fan-out). Aggregating each child table separately before joining fixes this. Interviewers often test whether you spot fan-out.

title: Short-circuit is not guaranteed
q: Return customers where the name has a space and the text before the first space is longer than 5 characters. Write it safely so CHARINDEX never gives a negative length.
sql:
SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName
FROM retail_logistics.Customers
WHERE CHARINDEX(' ', CustomerName) > 0
  AND LEN(LEFT(CustomerName, CASE WHEN CHARINDEX(' ', CustomerName) > 0
                                 THEN CHARINDEX(' ', CustomerName) - 1 ELSE 0 END)) > 5
ORDER BY CustomerName;

title: NOT IN and the NULL trap
q: Interview trap: show why NOT IN fails when the list contains NULL. Find shipments that are not a parent of any other shipment, first with NOT IN (wrong), then with NOT EXISTS (right).
sql:
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
   WHERE e.ShipmentID NOT IN (SELECT ParentShipmentID
                               FROM retail_logistics.Shipments)) AS NotIn_Wrong,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
   WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS c
                     WHERE c.ParentShipmentID = e.ShipmentID)) AS NotExists_Right;
how: ParentShipmentID is NULL on every row here. `x NOT IN (..., NULL)` is never true, so NOT IN returns 0. NOT EXISTS ignores the NULLs and correctly finds that no shipment is a parent. You can also fix NOT IN by adding `WHERE ParentShipmentID IS NOT NULL` inside the subquery.

q: Rank the 10 highest freight charges (1 = highest) using a correlated subquery instead of RANK().
sql:
SELECT TOP (10) e.ShipmentID, e.FreightCharge,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS x WHERE x.FreightCharge > e.FreightCharge) + 1 AS FreightChargeRank
FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
ORDER BY FreightChargeRank, e.ShipmentID;
how: Counting how many rows are higher, plus 1, gives the same result as RANK(). It is slower on large tables, but interviewers ask it to test understanding.

title: Top customer per region
q: Using only subqueries (no window functions), show the customer with the highest total freight charge in each region.
sql:
SELECT t.Region, t.CustomerName, t.Total
FROM (SELECT p.Region, p.CustomerName, SUM(e.FreightCharge) AS Total
      FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p
      JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e ON e.CustomerID = p.CustomerID
      GROUP BY p.Region, p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName) AS t
WHERE t.Total = (SELECT MAX(t2.Total)
                 FROM (SELECT p2.Region, SUM(e2.FreightCharge) AS Total
                       FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p2
                       JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e2 ON e2.CustomerID = p2.CustomerID
                       GROUP BY p2.Region, p2.CustomerID) AS t2
                 WHERE t2.Region = t.Region)
ORDER BY t.Region;
how: Per-customer totals are compared with the maximum total of the same region. It works, but the window-function version is shorter, which is a good point to make in an interview.

title: Shipments after a customer's first package
q: For each customer who has a package, count how many of their shipments happened after the shipment of their first package.
sql:
SELECT x.CustomerID, COUNT(e.ShipmentID) AS LaterShipments
FROM (SELECT e1.CustomerID, MIN(e1.ShipDate) AS FirstRxDate
      FROM retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS li
      JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e1 ON e1.ShipmentID = li.ShipmentID
      GROUP BY e1.CustomerID) AS x
LEFT JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
       ON e.CustomerID = x.CustomerID
      AND e.ShipDate > x.FirstRxDate
GROUP BY x.CustomerID
ORDER BY LaterShipments DESC, x.CustomerID;
how: The derived table finds each customer's first package date. The LEFT JOIN on a date condition counts the later shipments, and customers with none get 0.

title: IN vs EXISTS vs JOIN
q: Return customers with at least one Pending shipment three ways (IN, EXISTS, JOIN with DISTINCT). Each should return the same count.
sql:
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM retail_logistics.Customers
   WHERE CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
                       WHERE Status = 'Pending')) AS ViaIn,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p
   WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
                 WHERE e.CustomerID = p.CustomerID AND e.Status = 'Pending')) AS ViaExists,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.CustomerID)
   FROM retail_logistics.Customers AS p
   JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS e ON e.CustomerID = p.CustomerID
   WHERE e.Status = 'Pending') AS ViaJoin;
how: All three give the same answer. A plain JOIN repeats a customer for each matching shipment, which is why DISTINCT is needed. IN and EXISTS never duplicate rows.

title: Above their group's average
q: List shipments whose freight charge is more than the average freight charge of their own shipment type.
sql:
SELECT e.ShipmentID, e.ShipmentCategory, e.FreightCharge
FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
WHERE e.FreightCharge > (SELECT AVG(x.FreightCharge) FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS x
                  WHERE x.ShipmentCategory = e.ShipmentCategory)
ORDER BY e.ShipmentCategory, e.FreightCharge DESC, e.ShipmentID;
how: The correlated subquery calculates the average for the current row's type. AVG() OVER (PARTITION BY ...) is the window-function alternative.
